name: Rootly
description: Rootly incident management: incidents with timeline, action items and status page updates, alerts, services, functionalities, teams, severities and incident types, on-call (who is on call, schedules, shifts, escalation policies), status pages and retrospectives. Declare, update, mitigate and resolve incidents, acknowledge and resolve alerts.
instructions:
## Rootly
This connector works with **Rootly** incident management through its REST API (`https://api.rootly.com`, JSON:API): incidents with their timeline, action items and status page updates, alerts, the service catalog (services, functionalities, teams, environments, severities, incident types), users, on-call (who is on call, schedules, shifts, escalation policies), status pages and retrospectives. It can declare, update, mitigate and resolve incidents, add timeline notes and action items, acknowledge and resolve alerts and publish status page updates.

**Setup (2 minutes)**
1. In Rootly open the organization menu, **Organization Settings, API Keys** and create a key. A **Global** key sees the whole organization; a **Team** key only that team's records; a **Personal** key acts with your own permissions.
2. Give the key a role that can read what you need, plus write permission for incidents, alerts and action items if the agent should change them.
3. Paste the key into `ROOTLY_API_KEY` and run `rootly_get_current_user` to check it.

**Workflow**
- What is going on: `rootly_list_incidents` with `status: "started,mitigated"` (or `in_triage`), then `rootly_get_incident`, `rootly_list_incident_events` for the timeline and `rootly_list_incident_action_items`. Look up ids with `rootly_list_severities`, `rootly_list_services`, `rootly_get_service`, `rootly_list_functionalities`, `rootly_get_functionality`, `rootly_list_teams`, `rootly_get_team`, `rootly_list_environments`, `rootly_list_incident_types` and `rootly_list_users`.
- Run an incident: `rootly_create_incident` (pass an `idempotency_key`; use kind `test` for a try), `rootly_update_incident` for title, summary, severity, services or status, `rootly_add_incident_event` for timeline notes, then `rootly_mitigate_incident` and `rootly_resolve_incident`.
- Tasks and follow-ups: `rootly_list_action_items` across incidents, `rootly_get_action_item`, `rootly_create_action_item`, `rootly_update_action_item` (e.g. status done).
- Alerts: `rootly_list_alerts` (status triggered or open), `rootly_get_alert` for the raw payload, `rootly_acknowledge_alert`, `rootly_resolve_alert`.
- On-call: `rootly_list_oncalls` answers who is on call now (or in a window); `rootly_list_schedules`, `rootly_get_schedule`, `rootly_get_schedule_shifts`, `rootly_list_shifts` and `rootly_list_escalation_policies` for the details.
- Communicate: `rootly_list_status_pages`, `rootly_get_status_page`, `rootly_list_incident_status_page_events`, then `rootly_create_status_page_event` to publish an update.
- Learn: `rootly_list_retrospectives` and `rootly_get_retrospective`.

**Before writing**: a normal incident runs workflows, opens a Slack channel and can page people; a status page update is public and can e-mail subscribers. Confirm with the user first. A private incident cannot be made public again.

**Reading the answers**: JSON:API: records are in `data` (`id`, `type`, `attributes`, `relationships`), embedded records from `include` in `included`. Ids are UUIDs, except user ids (numbers). The human incident number is `attributes.sequential_id` (INC-123). Times are ISO 8601, in UTC unless a time zone is given. `rootly_list_incidents` and `rootly_list_alerts` return a compact set of attributes by default (`fields`); pass `fields: ""` for all of them. Zoom meeting passwords and host links are left out of incident answers.

**Paging**: lists return `meta` with `current_page`, `next_page` (null on the last page), `total_count` and `total_pages`; call again with `page_number`. Incidents and alerts also accept the cursor `page_after` from `meta.next_cursor`. Keep `page_size` small, Rootly records are large.

**Errors**: 401 means a wrong or revoked key, 403 a key whose role or team does not allow the call, 404 an unknown id or one outside the key's team, 422 a validation error whose `errors` name the field, 429 the rate limit (the `X-RateLimit-*` headers tell when it resets; wait and retry).
prerequisites: A Rootly account and an API key (Organization Settings, API Keys) with a role that allows the calls.

ROOTLY_API_KEY.label: API key
ROOTLY_API_KEY.help: Rootly, Organization Settings, API Keys: create a Global, Team or Personal key and copy it.
ROOTLY_API_KEY.patternMessage: Paste only the key, without Bearer in front and without spaces.

verifyHints.401: Rootly refused the key: it is wrong or was revoked. Create a new one under Organization Settings, API Keys.
verifyHints.403: The key works but its role or team does not allow this call. Use a Global key or give the key a role with the needed permission.
verifyHints.429: Rootly rate-limited the key. Wait a minute and try again.

tools.name: rootly_get_current_user
tools.description: Show the user the API key acts as: id, name, email, time zone and role. Use it to check the key; a Global or Team key answers with the user that created it.

tools.name: rootly_list_incidents
tools.description: List incidents, newest first by default: sequential id (the 123 in INC-123), title, status, kind, severity, services, teams, environments, incident types, URL and the lifecycle timestamps (started, detected, acknowledged, mitigated, resolved, closed). Filter by status, severity, service, team, environment, type, text and dates.

search.description: Free-text search in the title and summary.

status.description: Only incidents with this status. Several are comma-separated, e.g. `started,mitigated`. Values: in_triage, started, detected, acknowledged, mitigated, resolved, closed, cancelled; scheduled maintenance uses scheduled, in_progress, completed.

kind.description: Only this kind: normal, test, example, backfilled, scheduled (and their `_sub` forms for sub-incidents). Comma-separate several.

severity.description: Only this severity slug (e.g. `sev0`, `sev1`), from `rootly_list_severities`. Comma-separate several.

private.description: `true` for private incidents only, `false` for public only.

sequential_id.description: Only the incident with this number (the 123 in INC-123).

service_ids.description: Only incidents on these service ids (comma-separated), from `rootly_list_services`.

team_ids.description: Only incidents of these team ids (comma-separated), from `rootly_list_teams`.

environment_ids.description: Only incidents in these environment ids (comma-separated), from `rootly_list_environments`.

functionality_ids.description: Only incidents on these functionality ids (comma-separated), from `rootly_list_functionalities`.

type_ids.description: Only incidents of these incident type ids (comma-separated), from `rootly_list_incident_types`.

created_at_gte.description: Created at or after this ISO 8601 time, e.g. 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z.

created_at_lte.description: Created at or before this ISO 8601 time.

started_at_gte.description: Started at or after this ISO 8601 time.

started_at_lte.description: Started at or before this ISO 8601 time.

resolved_at_gte.description: Resolved at or after this ISO 8601 time.

updated_at_gte.description: Updated at or after this ISO 8601 time; use it to poll for changes.

include.description: Related records to embed in `included`, comma-separated, e.g. `roles,subscribers,action_items,events,custom_field_selections`. Leave empty for a compact answer.

fields.description: Incident attributes to return, comma-separated (JSON:API sparse fieldset). The default keeps the useful ones; pass an empty string to get every attribute.

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

page_size.description: Results per page (Rootly default 20). Keep it small (10 to 50): Rootly records are large.

page_after.description: Cursor for cursor paging: `meta.next_cursor` of the previous answer. Use either this or page_number.

tools.name: rootly_get_incident
tools.description: Get one incident with all its attributes: title, summary, status, severity, services, teams, environments, types, labels, Slack channel, linked tickets, mitigation and resolution messages and every timestamp. Add `include` for roles, subscribers, action items, events or custom fields.

include.description: Related records to embed in `included`, comma-separated: sub_statuses, causes, subscribers, roles, environments, incident_types, services, functionalities, groups, events, action_items, custom_field_selections, feedbacks, incident_post_mortem.

tools.name: rootly_create_incident
tools.description: Declare an incident. Without `kind` it is a normal incident: Rootly runs the workflows, creates the Slack channel and pages or notifies people as configured. Use kind `test` for a try. Set `idempotency_key` so a retry within 24 hours returns the same incident instead of opening a second one.

idempotency_key.description: A unique string for this request (e.g. a UUID). Repeating the call with the same key within 24 hours returns the incident already created.

title.description: Incident title. Rootly generates one when it is left empty on create.

labels.description: Labels as key and value pairs, e.g. {"region": "eu-west-1"}.

kind.description: normal (default), test, example, backfilled or scheduled (a maintenance window).

status.description: Starting status (default started). `in_triage` opens it in triage first.

private.description: Create a private incident, visible only to its members. A private incident cannot be made public again.

tools.name: rootly_update_incident
tools.description: Change an incident: title, summary, status, severity, affected services, functionalities, environments, types, teams, causes or labels. Only the fields you pass change; a list replaces the whole list (pass the current ids too when adding one). For mitigating and resolving with a message prefer `rootly_mitigate_incident` and `rootly_resolve_incident`.

title.description: Incident title. Rootly generates one when it is left empty on create.

labels.description: Labels as key and value pairs, e.g. {"region": "eu-west-1"}.

status.description: New status. Moving it on runs the workflows tied to that status.

public_title.description: Title shown on public status pages.

tools.name: rootly_mitigate_incident
tools.description: Mark an incident as mitigated (the impact is under control) with a short note on how. Sets `mitigated_at` and runs the mitigation workflows.

tools.name: rootly_resolve_incident
tools.description: Mark an incident as resolved with a short note on how. Sets `resolved_at`, runs the resolution workflows and usually starts the retrospective.

tools.name: rootly_list_incident_events
tools.description: List the timeline of an incident: the events (notes, status changes, updates) with their text, visibility (internal or external) and when they occurred.

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

page_size.description: Results per page (Rootly default 20). Keep it small (10 to 50): Rootly records are large.

tools.name: rootly_add_incident_event
tools.description: Add a note to the timeline of an incident. Internal notes stay with the responders; external ones can be shared.

event.description: The text of the timeline entry.

tools.name: rootly_list_action_items
tools.description: List action items across all incidents: summary, kind (task during the incident, follow_up after it), priority, status, assignee, due date and the incident. Filter by status, priority, kind, incident status and due date.

status.description: Only this status: open, in_progress, cancelled, done. Comma-separate several.

priority.description: Only this priority: high, medium, low.

incident_status.description: Only items of incidents in this status, e.g. resolved.

due_date_gte.description: Due on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO 8601).

due_date_lte.description: Due on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO 8601).

sort.description: Sort field, `-` for descending, e.g. `-created_at` or `due_date`.

include.description: Related records to embed, comma-separated, e.g. `incident`.

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

page_size.description: Results per page (Rootly default 20). Keep it small (10 to 50): Rootly records are large.

tools.name: rootly_list_incident_action_items
tools.description: List the action items of one incident: summary, kind, priority, status, assignee and due date.

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

page_size.description: Results per page (Rootly default 20). Keep it small (10 to 50): Rootly records are large.

tools.name: rootly_get_action_item
tools.description: Get one action item with its description, assignee, teams, due date and linked Jira issue.

tools.name: rootly_create_action_item
tools.description: Add an action item to an incident: a task to do now or a follow-up for after the incident, with priority, assignee and due date.

summary.description: Short summary of what to do.

kind.description: task (default, during the incident) or follow_up (after it).

assigned_to_user_id.description: Id of the user to assign, from `rootly_list_users` (a number).

tools.name: rootly_update_action_item
tools.description: Change an action item: summary, description, status (e.g. done), priority, assignee or due date. Only the fields you pass change.

kind.description: task (default, during the incident) or follow_up (after it).

assigned_to_user_id.description: Id of the user to assign, from `rootly_list_users` (a number).

tools.name: rootly_list_alerts
tools.description: List alerts, newest first: short id, summary, status (open, triggered, acknowledged, resolved, deferred), source (datadog, grafana, email and so on), noise flag, services, teams, environments, urgency and timestamps. Filter by status, source, service, team, environment, labels and dates.

status.description: Only this status: open, triggered, acknowledged, resolved, deferred. Comma-separate several.

source.description: Only alerts from this source, e.g. datadog, grafana, prometheus, email, api.

services.description: Only alerts on these service ids (comma-separated).

groups.description: Only alerts of these team ids (comma-separated).

environments.description: Only alerts in these environment ids (comma-separated).

labels.description: Only alerts with these labels, `key:value`, comma-separated.

started_at_gte.description: Started at or after this ISO 8601 time.

started_at_lte.description: Started at or before this ISO 8601 time.

created_at_gte.description: Created at or after this ISO 8601 time.

include.description: Related records to embed, comma-separated, e.g. `incidents,services,responders`.

fields.description: Alert attributes to return, comma-separated. The default leaves out the raw payload (`data`); pass an empty string for every attribute.

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

page_size.description: Results per page (Rootly default 20). Keep it small (10 to 50): Rootly records are large.

page_after.description: Cursor for cursor paging: `meta.next_cursor` of the previous answer. Use either this or page_number.

tools.name: rootly_get_alert
tools.description: Get one alert with its full details, including the raw payload the source sent (`data`), labels, responders and linked incidents.

include.description: Related records to embed, comma-separated, e.g. `incidents,events,responders`.

tools.name: rootly_acknowledge_alert
tools.description: Acknowledge an alert: someone is looking at it, so its escalation stops paging the next level. Recorded as done by the API key.

tools.name: rootly_resolve_alert
tools.description: Resolve an alert, optionally with a note and also resolving the incidents it is attached to.

resolve_related_incidents.description: Also resolve the incidents this alert is attached to.

tools.name: rootly_list_services
tools.description: List the services in the catalog: name, slug, description, owners, linked repositories and external ids (Backstage, Cortex, OpsLevel, PagerDuty).

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

page_size.description: Results per page (Rootly default 20). Keep it small (10 to 50): Rootly records are large.

tools.name: rootly_get_service
tools.description: Get one service with its description, owner teams and users, escalation policy, alert and incident broadcast settings and external links.

tools.name: rootly_list_functionalities
tools.description: List the functionalities (user-facing capabilities such as Checkout or Login) with name, slug, description and owners.

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

page_size.description: Results per page (Rootly default 20). Keep it small (10 to 50): Rootly records are large.

tools.name: rootly_get_functionality
tools.description: Get one functionality with its description, owners, linked services and status page components.

tools.name: rootly_list_teams
tools.description: List the teams (groups) with name, slug, description, members and their on-call and escalation settings.

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

page_size.description: Results per page (Rootly default 20). Keep it small (10 to 50): Rootly records are large.

tools.name: rootly_get_team
tools.description: Get one team with its description and members; add `include` for its schedules and escalation policies.

tools.name: rootly_list_environments
tools.description: List the environments (production, staging and so on) with name, slug and colour.

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

page_size.description: Results per page (Rootly default 20). Keep it small (10 to 50): Rootly records are large.

tools.name: rootly_list_severities
tools.description: List the severity levels (e.g. SEV0 to SEV3) with id, name, slug, level (`severity`: critical, high, medium, low), description and colour. Use the id when creating or updating incidents.

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

page_size.description: Results per page (Rootly default 20). Keep it small (10 to 50): Rootly records are large.

tools.name: rootly_list_incident_types
tools.description: List the incident types (e.g. Security, Customer facing) with id, name, slug and description.

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

page_size.description: Results per page (Rootly default 20). Keep it small (10 to 50): Rootly records are large.

tools.name: rootly_list_users
tools.description: List the users of the organization: id, name, email, time zone; add `include` for role, teams or schedules.

search.description: Free-text search in name and email.

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

page_size.description: Results per page (Rootly default 20). Keep it small (10 to 50): Rootly records are large.

tools.name: rootly_list_oncalls
tools.description: Who is on call: the on-call entries of every escalation policy, schedule and level for now or a time window, with the user, schedule, escalation policy and level. Filter by schedule, escalation policy, user, service or team.

since.description: Start of the window, ISO 8601 (default now).

until.description: End of the window, ISO 8601 (default the same as since).

earliest.description: Only the first on-call entry per escalation policy path and level.

time_zone.description: Time zone for the times in the answer, e.g. Europe/Berlin (default UTC).

tools.name: rootly_list_schedules
tools.description: List the on-call schedules with name, description, owning teams and time zone.

team_ids.description: Only schedules of these team ids, comma-separated.

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

page_size.description: Results per page (Rootly default 20). Keep it small (10 to 50): Rootly records are large.

tools.name: rootly_get_schedule
tools.description: Get one on-call schedule with its owners, time zone and settings.

tools.name: rootly_get_schedule_shifts
tools.description: List the shifts of one schedule in a time window: who is on call from when to when, including overrides.

tools.name: rootly_list_shifts
tools.description: List on-call shifts across schedules in a time window (default: the shifts running now): schedule, rotation, user, start and end, override and shadow flags. Filter by schedule and user.

from.description: Start of the window, ISO 8601 (default now).

user_ids.description: Only these user ids (numbers as text).

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

tools.name: rootly_list_escalation_policies
tools.description: List the escalation policies with name, description, repeat settings and owning teams; add `include` for their levels and paths.

team_ids.description: Only policies of these team ids, comma-separated.

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

page_size.description: Results per page (Rootly default 20). Keep it small (10 to 50): Rootly records are large.

tools.name: rootly_list_status_pages
tools.description: List the status pages with title, public URL, whether they are public, and their settings.

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

page_size.description: Results per page (Rootly default 20). Keep it small (10 to 50): Rootly records are large.

tools.name: rootly_get_status_page
tools.description: Get one status page with its title, description, public URL, components and settings.

tools.name: rootly_list_incident_status_page_events
tools.description: List the updates an incident published to status pages: text, status (investigating, identified, monitoring, resolved), status page and time.

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

page_size.description: Results per page (Rootly default 20). Keep it small (10 to 50): Rootly records are large.

tools.name: rootly_create_status_page_event
tools.description: Publish an incident update on a status page, e.g. Investigating, then Identified, Monitoring and Resolved. It is public and can notify the page subscribers.

event.description: The update text shown on the page.

status.description: investigating (default), identified, monitoring or resolved; scheduled maintenance uses scheduled, in_progress or completed.

notify_subscribers.description: Notify the subscribers of the status page (default false).

tools.name: rootly_list_retrospectives
tools.description: List incident retrospectives (post-mortems): title, status (draft, published), the incident, URL and dates. Filter by status, severity, team, service and dates.

severity.description: Only retrospectives of incidents with this severity slug.

created_at_gte.description: Created at or after this ISO 8601 time.

created_at_lte.description: Created at or before this ISO 8601 time.

page_number.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default 1). `meta.next_page` of the previous answer gives the next one; it is null on the last page.

page_size.description: Results per page (Rootly default 20). Keep it small (10 to 50): Rootly records are large.

tools.name: rootly_get_retrospective
tools.description: Get one retrospective with its title, status, content, URL and the incident it belongs to.
